who: Sidney Bradshaw Fay, historian of European diplomacy at Harvard and Radcliffe, PhD Harvard 1900.

evidence.says: Identifies Sidney Bradshaw Fay as the author of The Rise of Brandenburg-Prussia to 1786, also publishing as Sidney B. Fay.
Reports a Harvard PhD in 1900 and appointment as professor at Harvard and Radcliffe in 1929; retirement in 1945.
The AHA identifies Sidney B. Fay as Sidney Bradshaw Fay and places his Harvard/Radcliffe service in 1929–1946.

notes: Exact doctoral institution and year match. This establishes identity, not independent confirmation of the listed 1949 supervision.

who: Michael George Finlayson, historian of seventeenth-century England at the University of Toronto, PhD Toronto.

evidence.says: Links Michael George Finlayson to Michael G. Finlayson, author of Historians, Puritanism, and the English Revolution, in Toronto's History Department.
Lists M. G. Finlayson in History among graduate faculty and members emeriti, including the History faculty list on printed page 367.
The faculty association's history, printed page 79, identifies Michael Finlayson as having completed his PhD in History at Toronto.

notes: Institution, period and doctoral institution agree. The alternative LC candidate n92806435 is identified with psychology and psychiatry.

who: Nels W. Forde, ancient historian at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, PhD Minnesota 1964.

evidence.says: Identifies Nels W. Forde as the author of Nebraska Cuneiform Texts of the Sumerian Ur III Dynasty (1972).
Professional memorials report his Minnesota PhD in 1964 and Nebraska teaching in 1960–1965 and 1967–1994; publications include Nebraska Cuneiform Texts and Cato the Censor.
Nebraska's repository names Nels W. Forde as advisor of a 1973 History thesis on criminal justice in ancient Judaea.

notes: The authority's publication matches the professor's bibliography; doctorate and Nebraska appointment cover the supplied student record.

who: Brett V. Gadsden, historian of twentieth-century American and African American history at Northwestern, PhD Northwestern 2006.

evidence.says: Establishes the heading Brett V. Gadsden and records Brett Gadsden as a publication name.
Brett V. Gadsden's CV gives a History PhD from Northwestern in December 2006 and a Northwestern faculty appointment beginning September 2017.
The 2026 commencement program lists Alex Keith's dissertation on Black women and diaspora in London and Chicago theater, with Brett Gadsden as adviser.

notes: Full publication name, exact doctorate and the supplied student/adviser relationship agree.

who: Thomas W. Ganschow, historian of modern China at the University of Georgia, PhD Indiana 1971.

evidence.says: Identifies Thomas Ganschow as an emeritus Georgia history professor with an Indiana PhD and research on Sun Yat-sen.
Identifies Thomas W. Ganschow, also Thomas William Ganschow, through his 1971 study of Sun Yat-sen's contacts with the United States.
Bibliographic entry 315 identifies Thomas W. Ganschow's A Study of Sun Yat-sen's Contacts with the United States Prior to 1922 as an Indiana University PhD, 1971.
The other Thomas Ganschow authority concerns a classical archaeologist and numismatist, author of Untersuchungen zur Baugeschichte in Herculaneum.

notes: The Georgia historian matches the doctoral record and Chinese-history field; the archaeologist is a different candidate.

who: Ellen Garrison, historian and archival educator at Middle Tennessee State University, PhD in History Stanford.

evidence.says: The indexed retirement notice identifies Ellen Garrison as an MTSU history faculty member and archival educator with MA and PhD degrees in History from Stanford; the newsletter also names Tom Kanon alongside her.
Graduate Council minutes record Ellen Garrison, History, receiving doctoral graduate faculty membership in October 2007.
The Ellen Garrison authority is established from Archives in Appalachia (1985).
The publisher identifies Ellen Garrison as editor of Archives in Appalachia: A Directory (1985), an archival reference work.

notes: Matching name, archival specialization, Stanford doctorate and MTSU doctoral faculty service support the identification. The old newsletter URL now returns 404; its text remains search-indexed.

who: Kent B. Germany, historian of the American South and presidential politics at the University of South Carolina, PhD Tulane 2000.

evidence.says: Identifies Kent B. Germany as an editor of the Lyndon B. Johnson presidential recordings.
Kent B. Germany's CV gives a PhD in History from Tulane in December 2000 and publications editing the Johnson recordings.
Identifies Kent Germany as a South Carolina history professor, Tulane History PhD and scholar working with the Presidential Recordings Program.
Thomas Lekan's CV lists Caroline Peyton's completed 2016 Radioactive Dixie dissertation and identifies its advisor as Kent Germany.

notes: Authority works, full CV name, exact doctorate and supplied supervision agree.

who: August W. Giebelhaus, historian of technology and business at Georgia Tech, PhD Delaware.

evidence.says: Identifies August W. Giebelhaus, author of Business and Government in the Oil Industry, explicitly affiliated with Georgia Institute of Technology.
The retirement notice on printed page 11 identifies August Giebelhaus as a Georgia Tech history professor with a Delaware PhD, serving from 1976 until retirement after 33 years.

notes: The authority explicitly gives the student's institution; the doctoral institution and faculty service through 2002 also agree.
